questions.stem: A pressure group differs from other associations mainly because it

options.text: seeks to win a majority of seats in the legislature
seeks to influence government policy without itself forming government
is always violent in its methods
must be registered with INEC as a political party

questions.explanation: The defining aim is influence, not office. A pressure group organises members around an interest or a cause and then lobbies, publicises or withholds cooperation until policy moves in its direction. Forming government is the work of a party.

distractorRationale.a: Winning legislative seats is what a political party exists to do
distractorRationale.c: Most recognised pressure groups operate by lawful methods; violence is not part of the definition
distractorRationale.d: INEC registration as a party would turn the association into a political party

questions.stem: The Manufacturers Association of Nigeria (MAN) is best classified as

options.text: a promotional or cause group
an interest or sectional group
an anomic group
a political party

questions.explanation: MAN exists to defend the material interests of its own members — Nigerian manufacturers — on tariffs, power supply, tax and credit. That makes it an interest or sectional group, and an associational one because it has a formal constitution and officials. It does not exist to promote a cause for society at large, nor does it contest elections.

distractorRationale.a: A promotional group campaigns for a cause (the environment, human rights) rather than members' profits
distractorRationale.c: An anomic group is a spontaneous, unorganised outburst, which MAN is not
distractorRationale.d: MAN does not canvass for votes or seek to form government

questions.stem: The most important distinction between a pressure group and a political party is that

options.text: only political parties may hold public meetings
pressure groups seek to form government while parties do not
political parties seek to form government while pressure groups do not
pressure groups must have members in every state of the federation

questions.explanation: A party asks the electorate for the right to govern. A pressure group asks those who already govern to change a policy. Section 221 of the 1999 Constitution even forbids any association that is not a party from canvassing for votes. Methods, membership and breadth of programme all follow from that difference of aim.

distractorRationale.a: Section 40 of the Constitution guarantees peaceful assembly to every person, not only to parties
distractorRationale.b: This reverses the distinction and would score zero
distractorRationale.d: National spread is a constitutional requirement for parties, not for pressure groups

questions.stem: Which of the following is a method commonly used by the Nigeria Labour Congress to influence government?

options.text: Registering candidates for the Senate
Declaring a nationwide strike
Dissolving a State House of Assembly
Appointing ministers of labour

questions.explanation: The strike — withdrawal of labour — is labour's classic instrument. Combined with collective bargaining, publicity and the threat of further action, it has been used by the NLC over wages, fuel prices and labour law. The other options are powers of parties or of constitutional organs, not of a union.

distractorRationale.a: Only a registered political party may present candidates for the National Assembly
distractorRationale.c: Dissolving a House of Assembly is not a power of any pressure group
distractorRationale.d: Ministers are appointed by the President, subject to Senate confirmation

questions.stem: A pressure group is likely to have the greatest influence on government when

options.text: its members occupy a strategic position in the economy and it is united
it has no funds and no access to the media
it is unknown to the public and has a divided leadership
it seeks to replace the Constitution by force

questions.explanation: Influence is a product of leverage. Oil workers, doctors or power-sector staff can halt essential services; a united leadership can deliver that threat credibly; public sympathy makes it costly for government to ignore them. Funds, expertise and lawful methods reinforce the same advantage. A poor, divided or extra-legal group loses that leverage.

distractorRationale.b: Poverty and silence remove the means of publicity and bargaining
distractorRationale.c: Obscurity and internal division are classic reasons a group fails
distractorRationale.d: Seeking to overthrow the Constitution is insurrection, not pressure-group activity, and destroys legitimacy

questions.stem: The Nigerian Bar Association is a promotional pressure group because it exists only to defend human rights for the whole of society.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: False. The NBA is primarily an interest or professional group: it exists to protect lawyers' professional interests and the independence of the bar. It does take up promotional causes — the rule of law, human rights — but that secondary activity does not reclassify it. Examiners treat the NBA, NMA and NLC as sectional/interest groups.

distractorRationale.a: Campaigns for the rule of law are real, but they do not cancel the NBA's identity as a professional interest group
